bib.title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors
bib.venue: NIPS 2017 (31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can the encoder of an attentional machine translation model be transferred as a reusable, contextual word representation that improves a range of downstream NLP tasks beyond pretrained word vectors?
hypothesis: MT data holds potential comparable to ImageNet as a cornerstone for reusable models; more MT training data should give more useful encoders.
contributions: CoVe: context vectors from the two-layer BiLSTM encoder of an English-German attentional seq2seq MT model, concatenated with GloVe as input to task models
A biattentive classification network (BCN) for single- and two-sentence classification
Evidence across sentiment, question classification, entailment and QA that CoVe helps, and that more MT data gives larger gains
State-of-the-art SST-5 and SNLI test results with the baseline model

method.summary: Train a 2-layer BiLSTM encoder inside an attentional seq2seq En-De MT model on one of three MT datasets (frozen GloVe inputs), then freeze it and concatenate its per-token outputs (CoVe) with GloVe (and optionally character n-gram vectors) as inputs to a biattentive classifier (BCN) or a Dynamic Coattention Network for SQuAD.
method.task: transfer learning from machine translation to sentiment, question classification, entailment and extractive QA

datasets.name: MT-Large (WMT 2017 news)
datasets.source: web crawl, news commentary, Europarl, EU press releases, En-De

datasets.name: SST-2
datasets.split: all sub-trees with length greater than 3 used for training

models.name: MT-LSTM (CoVe encoder), inside attentional seq2seq En-De
models.architecture: 2-layer bidirectional LSTM encoder; 2-layer unidirectional LSTM decoder with attention, based on OpenNMT (Klein et al. 2017)
models.init_from: fixed GloVe CommonCrawl-840B 300-d inputs; target embeddings random

models.name: BCN (biattentive classification network)
models.architecture: ReLU feedforward + BiLSTM encoder, biattention, one-layer BiLSTM integration, max/mean/min/self-attentive pooling, 3-layer batch-normalized maxout

models.name: DCN + Char + CoVe
models.architecture: Dynamic Coattention Network with tanh function g in place of ReLU f

models.name: Skip-thought vectors (4800-d)
models.architecture: unsupervised sentence encoder, Kiros et al. 2015

training.objective: MT: cross-entropy over target words (attentional seq2seq); downstream: supervised classification / QA span loss with MT-LSTM and word vectors frozen
training.lr: MT-LSTM: 1 initially, halved each epoch after validation perplexity first increased; downstream: alpha = 0.001
training.lr_schedule: MT-LSTM: halve each epoch after validation perplexity first increases
training.dropout: MT: 0.2 on inputs and outputs of all encoder and decoder layers; downstream: 0.1, 0.2 or 0.3 before all feedforward layers
training.regularisation: GloVe and MT-LSTM frozen during downstream training

other.maxout: pool over 4 channels, reduce dimensionality by 2, 4 or 8, reduce again by 2, project to output dimension
other.char_vectors: character n-gram embeddings of Hashimoto et al. 2016
other.dropout_choice: ratio chosen among 0.1/0.2/0.3 (selection procedure not stated)

inference.samples: single reported run per configuration; no seeds or variance stated

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: uncased, tokenized BLEU on MT test sets

eval.protocol: Validation numbers for ablations (Table 2); test numbers for best validation model per classification task (Table 4); SQuAD only on dev (Table 3). One run each, no significance tests.

availability.code: https://github.com/salesforce/cove (PyTorch example generating CoVe from the MT-LSTM used in best models)
availability.weights: MT-LSTM released via the same repository

results.claim: CoVe-L plus GloVe and char vectors lifts SQuAD dev F1 well above random vectors.
DCN+Char+CoVe beats published R-NET on SQuAD validation EM and F1.
results.setup: SQuAD dev, single model; not submitted for test
results.note: R-NET 71.1 EM, 79.5 F1; ours 79.9 F1. Baseline DCN+Char 65.4 EM, 75.6 F1.

results.claim: CoVe pushes the SNLI baseline to a new state of the art on test.
CoVe pushes SST-5 fine-grained sentiment to a new state of the art on test.
Larger MT training set gives larger gains: SQuAD F1 rises with CoVe-S, -M, -L.
SST-2 validation accuracy with GloVe+CoVe-L vs GloVe alone.
CoVe beats character n-grams as an addition to GloVe on SST-2 and SQuAD, and combining both is best.
results.note: GloVe+Char 90.1; SQuAD 79.9 vs 78.1. On TREC-6 Char (94.7) is below GloVe (94.9).

results.claim: CoVe-L outperforms skip-thought vectors on SST-2 validation.
MT-Large En-De encoder BLEU on WMT 2016 test.
results.quote: The MT-LSTM trained on MT-Large obtains an uncased, tokenized BLEU score of 28.96 on the WMT 2016 test set.

results.claim: MT-Small encoder BLEU on Multi30k 2016 test.
results.note: Highest BLEU is on the simplest, restricted-domain dataset.
results.quote: The MT-LSTM trained on MT-Small obtains an uncased, tokenized BLEU score of 38.5 on the Multi30k test set from 2016.

results.claim: MT-Medium encoder BLEU on IWSLT 2014 test.
results.quote: The model trained on MT-Medium obtains an uncased, tokenized BLEU score of 25.54 on the IWSLT test set from 2014.

results.claim: BCN+Char+CoVe IMDb test accuracy; below several published models (e.g. oh-LSTM 94.1).
TREC-6 test accuracy is below several published models, and TREC-50 is below rules-based systems.
results.note: Best published TREC-6 here: LSTM-CNN 96.1; TREC-50 ours 90.2 vs Rules 97.2.

limits: Only English-German MT tested; no other source tasks or language pairs.
Single runs, no seeds, variance or significance reported; compute, batch size, epochs and MT parameter counts not stated.
Gains are modest on small-delta tasks (e.g. SNLI 87.7 to 88.1 validation, TREC-6 94.9 to 95.8) and not SOTA on IMDb, TREC.
SQuAD result is validation only; not submitted for test.
The correlation between MT data size and downstream gain confounds data size with domain and language complexity (only three points).
CoVe is frozen features, not fine-tuned; later contextual LM pretraining with fine-tuning supersedes it (not in the paper).
